- Policy stance: The FOMC raised the funds rate to 1.5–1.75%, signaled ongoing hikes, and continued balance-sheet runoff (Treasury $30B/MBS $17.5B caps in June–July). Desk settings (e.g., ON RRP 1.55%) tighten conditions. Inflation risks remain elevated from pandemic imbalances, energy, Ukraine war, and China lockdowns.
- SLOOS read-through: Domestic banks reported stronger loan demand for C&I purposes (inventory, A/R, plant and equipment) while standards on C&I were not broadly tight and in some cases eased; foreign banks tightened C&I standards. In CRE, domestic standards were eased for multifamily and largely unchanged for construction/land development and nonfarm nonresidential. In household credit, banks eased standards on credit cards; demand strengthened for HELOCs and autos but weakened for RRE mortgages.
- Implications: While the Fed’s hawkish tightening and FSR-flagged vulnerabilities pose growth and market-risk headwinds, SLOOS indicates bank credit supply remains available in key segments with healthy demand, tempering near-term downside risks.
- Net assessment: Hawkish and credibility-positive on inflation, but with less negative growth impulse than otherwise implied by policy/FSR alone.
